pll2d1c2-d1e3514.summary: Distinguishes: to create is properly to make something from nothing; to make is also to work from matter. So humans or angels are makers or craftsmen but not creators; God alone, who makes from nothing and from something, properly bears the name creator, though he shares the other names with creatures and Scripture often uses them interchangeably.
claims: Creatures can make but not create.

pl-l2d1c2.summary: Distinguishes 'create' from 'make': to create is properly to make something from nothing; to make is also to work from matter. So humans and angels make but do not create; 'creator' belongs properly to God alone, who makes some things from nothing and some from something, though Scripture often uses 'create' and 'make' interchangeably.
claims: To create is properly to make from nothing.
To make includes working from matter.
Humans and angels make but do not create.
Scripture often uses 'create' and 'make' without distinction.
